title: SMI and CEUS in the Diagnosis of Benign Focal Liver Lesions: Comparison of Diagnostic Accuracy Considering Examiner Experience
summary:
This study evaluates and compares the diagnostic accuracy of two ultrasound modalities—SMI (Superb Microvascular Imaging) and CEUS (contrast-enhanced ultrasound)—in the diagnosis of benign liver lesions, with a primary focus on analyzing the impact of examiner experience on diagnostic quality. To achieve this, the diagnostic accuracy for three specific liver lesions will be determined depending on the ultrasound modality used.
Benign liver lesions, such as hemangiomas, focal nodular hyperplasias, and adenomas, are common incidental findings during routine ultrasound examinations. Their precise differentiation is crucial for subsequent clinical management, particularly in the presence of patient-specific risk factors or an atypical appearance on standard gray-scale ultrasound. In such cases, both Superb Microvascular Imaging (SMI) and contrast-enhanced ultrasound (CEUS) provide valuable additional information compared to conventional ultrasound, thereby facilitating the differentiation between benign and malignant liver lesions. To date, CEUS—alongside radiological imaging modalities such as CT or MRI—is considered the gold standard for evaluating complex liver lesions. SMI is an innovative Doppler ultrasound technique that utilizes a novel algorithm to filter out motion artifacts, enabling the visualization of lesion vascular architecture without the administration of a contrast agent. Consequently, SMI offers the potential to be a cost-effective, infinitely repeatable, and lower-risk alternative to CEUS.
However, it has not yet been systematically investigated how SMI affects the diagnostic accuracy for benign liver lesions depending on examiner experience. Furthermore, an evaluation of the learning curve for interpreting SMI findings compared to CEUS findings in ultrasound-naive individuals is currently lacking. To investigate this impact, we aim to divide the research project into a physician group and a student group. Both groups will evaluate ultrasound patient cases using a questionnaire, the analysis of which will allow us to compare diagnostic accuracy.

interventions.name: Analysis of the impact of examiner experience on the diagnostic accuracy of two ultrasound modalities for the diagnosis of benign focal liver lesions based on retrospectively collected patient data.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
-Patients with an ultrasonographically visualized benign liver lesion
-Gastroenterology colleagues with basic or advanced understanding of contrast-enhanced ultrasound (CEUS)
-Medical students at Heinrich Heine University who have completed their second year of study and successfully participated in the faculty-internal elective course "Basic Abdominal Ultrasound"
Exclusion criteria:
-Gastroenterology colleagues without prior experience in contrast-enhanced ultrasound (CEUS).
-Students who have not completed their second year of study and/or have not successfully completed the elective course "Basic Abdominal Ultrasound".
